Endocrinology · published research

Hypothyroidism

Some sham-controlled studies found improved quality-of-life or symptom measures, and one trial cohort used less levothyroxine over follow-up. Other controlled results found no between-group change in thyroid function or autoimmunity.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Some sham-controlled studies found improved quality-of-life or symptom measures, and one trial cohort used less levothyroxine over follow-up. Other controlled results found no between-group change in thyroid function or autoimmunity.

Summary of the Evidence

Thirteen exact-category publications comprise two reviews, ten human papers, and one mouse experiment. The ten human publications likely represent about five clinical datasets rather than ten separate trials: four Höfling reports follow one 43-person randomized study, and possible overlap also exists among reports from other groups. The publication count therefore should not be read as ten independent confirmations.

Human and clinical evidence

In the original sham-controlled Höfling trial, PBM-treated participants had lower thyroid-peroxidase antibody levels, improved ultrasound echogenicity, and a lower levothyroxine requirement during follow-up. A six-year report from the same cohort found that levothyroxine requirements remained lower in the active-treatment group, while anti-TPO and anti-thyroglobulin antibody levels no longer differed. This is follow-up of the original trial, not an independent replication (Höfling et al. 2013 long-term follow-up, Source).

A separate 46-person sham-controlled study reported better quality of life and several oxidative-stress measures with laser treatment, but found no between-group change in thyroid function or autoimmunity at three months (Tunç et al. 2024). A later randomized report found improvement in fatigue and other symptom scores, although the database does not establish whether its participants overlap with earlier reports (Tunç et al. 2026). These findings support symptom and quality-of-life outcomes more directly than restoration of thyroid hormone production.

Animal evidence

One propylthiouracil-induced hypothyroid mouse experiment found no measurable restoration of thyroid function after PBM. It is a single preclinical study and does not resolve the mixed human findings.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No exact-category in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified in the records reviewed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The Höfling protocol used 830-nm near-infrared laser light at 50 mW and 707 J/cm², delivered for 40 seconds per point over ten sessions, twice weekly for five weeks. Later controlled studies used their own protocols, and the available reports do not compare wavelengths or doses directly. Medication was adjusted according to thyroid tests in the clinical studies, so lower replacement dose does not by itself demonstrate hormone-independent recovery.

Interpretation

Clinical results include lower levothyroxine requirements in one trial cohort and improved quality-of-life or symptom measures in other sham-controlled reports. The 46-person trial did not find a short-term change in thyroid function or autoimmunity, and the long-term dose report belongs to the original cohort. Thus, the patient-reported outcomes are more consistently favorable than evidence for restored thyroid function or remission.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for short-term quality-of-life or symptom improvement Low for reduced levothyroxine requirements Very low for restored thyroid function or disease remission
Publications and records13 articles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Sham-controlled reports found better quality-of-life scores and some symptom improvement, while one earlier trial and its follow-up reported lower levothyroxine requirements. Several publications reuse the same patient group, and other trials did not find between-group hormone or antibody changes. Independent studies with clear medication rules and longer biochemical follow-up would strengthen these separate conclusions.
